tier_definitions.source_mapped: A reviewed native source owner is identified; no instruction equivalence is implied.
tier_definitions.review_classified: A reviewed block has an understood purpose and category, but receives instruction-accounting credit only when its native representation is also cited.
tier_definitions.instruction_accounted: The purpose of each listed original basic block is explicitly represented by cited native source.
tier_definitions.structurally_verified: A listed original CFG edge has an explicitly verified native semantic counterpart.
tier_definitions.native_checkpoint_observed: The native self-test executed the mapped semantic function checkpoint.
tier_definitions.original_trace_equivalent: An original-game trace and native semantic trace agree for a declared scenario.
tier_definitions.binary_matching: A MIPS build matches the original instruction words exactly.

functions.name: Frontend_PatchTeamPalette
functions.accounting_basis: All eleven blocks are semantically represented. The first six select the team palette and copy exactly 160 PS1 colors; tools/decode_team_backgrounds.py performs that substitution locally and loadTeamRosterBackgrounds validates the resulting native RGBA strips. The final five snapshot the patched palette into two transition buffers and initialize both counters to 16; RosterViewer::scanTeam retains the source/target teams and renderRosterViewer advances the equivalent 0..16 crossfade at the recovered 17 ms frontend tick. Pointer arithmetic, BGR555 scratch buffers, and MIPS copy loops are native replacements rather than emulated operations.

block_classifications.summary: Team/palette selection, address calculation, and the 160-entry PS1 CLUT copy are replaced by local mixed-palette decoding plus validated native RGBA loading.
The original two palette snapshots and counters initialized to 16 are represented by retained source/target teams and a native factor progressing from 0 through 16 at 17 ms per frontend tick.

functions.name: Rosters_ResolveTeamSlots
functions.accounting_basis: All ten blocks are semantically represented. RosterDatabase::resolveTeamSlots rejects teams outside the recovered 0..28 range, traverses exactly fifteen fixed slots, maps the signed -1 sentinel to null, resolves ordinary IDs through the native player index, and stores one result per slot. The stat-index-zero special-mode branch reproduces FUN_8005768C: it derives one of five rating tiers from the first four player ratings, combines it with the five-position index, reads the corresponding player ID from the private 5x5 FALL table, and resolves that replacement. tools/extract_roster_database.py streams both the 29x15 roster IDs and copyrighted fallback IDs from the user's local FEONLY.BIN; no game data is embedded in public source. The native self-test covers all 435 slots, both bounds, null slots, ordinary resolution, and the special fallback path.

block_classifications.summary: MIPS prologue/epilogue and the signed team bound are represented by a value-returning native function with explicit safe rejection outside team IDs 0..28.
The fixed fifteen-slot address arithmetic, -1/null branch, ordinary FUN_8005FE14 lookup, result store, and loop are represented by the fixed-size ResolvedTeamSlots traversal and native player index.
The global special-mode check, regular-stat-index-zero test, and FUN_8005768C replacement call are represented by the recovered position/rating-tier calculation over the local-only 5x5 FALL table.

functions.name: Rosters_CopySlotTable
functions.accounting_basis: All five blocks are semantically represented at this function boundary. tools/extract_roster_database.py streams the contiguous source layout from the user's private FEONLY.BIN into fixed TEAM and FREE sections. RosterDatabase::copySlotTable walks 29 teams with exactly fifteen signed slots, resolves each completed team through Rosters_ResolveTeamSlots, then consumes exactly 100 signed free-agent slots. It reproduces the FUN_80054CBC membership/count effect by assigning owners 0..28 for team players, owner 29 for the 67 listed free agents, and -1 for the 64 hidden/unlisted players while retaining 33 trailing holes. Finally it preserves the original +0x72E invalidation and FUN_8005DB34 invocation boundary as a derived-team-rating dirty request; the callee's internal rating/ranking algorithm remains separately scoped and is not claimed as part of this caller. Native tests cover all 535 copied slots, membership counts, terminator ordering, hidden players, and the post-copy dirty state.

block_classifications.summary: The MIPS prologue, global-context fetch, private source-table base, and zeroed loop counters are replaced by native fixed-size containers initialized by the local pack loader.
The nested 29-by-15 signed-short copy and per-team FUN_8005770C call are represented by copySlotTable's fixed team traversal and resolved_team_slots_ assignment.
The second exact 100-short copy loop is represented by the private FREE pack section and fixed free_agent_slots_ container, including 67 IDs and 33 trailing -1 holes.

FUN_80054CBC's roster-owner/count refresh is represented directly, while the +0x72E reset and FUN_8005DB34 call boundary become an explicit derived-rating dirty request. FUN_8005DB34 internals are not claimed here.

functions.name: Rosters_ConstructViewer
functions.accounting_basis: All seven blocks are semantically represented. RosterViewer::constructViewer retains the selected team index as the native replacement for the raw team-slot pointer; selectedTeam/renderRosterViewer resolve that ownership through the injected RosterDatabase. Every construction resets the six descriptor defaults recovered from DAT_800A4088 (0,15,32,32,44,44), initializes layer limit 3 and normal layer 2, and implements the original active-special branch by selecting special_stat_layer+3 and matching the limit. It records the descriptor count 28, current descriptor index, paired param_2 object-state flags, zero controller phase, and the exact FUN_80039D88 binding tuple (slot 0x12, flags 0x10004, object 0x11, value 7). Native tests cover normal, reopen/reset, active-special, inactive-special, both object flags, descriptor selection, phase reset, and controller binding.

block_classifications.summary: Raw roster-table pointer derivation becomes retained team identity plus database injection; the six-iteration descriptor-default copy becomes an explicit six-element reset on every construction.
Default layer 2/limit 3 and the active-special condition selecting global layer+3 are represented by RosterViewerConstructionContext and tested across both branch outcomes.

Descriptor count/index/pointer ownership, global viewer ownership, controller phase reset, paired object flags, and FUN_80039D88 object construction are represented as typed viewer state with the exact recovered binding constants.

functions.name: Rosters_RunViewer
functions.accounting_basis: All ten blocks are semantically represented at this orchestration boundary. RosterViewer::runViewer repairs saved player -1 by resetting player/window to zero, restores the two saved selection fields, normalizes team sentinel 29 to the active team when frontend mode is 2 or to team 3 otherwise, and calls the recovered constructor with the active special-layer context. It records the exact generic input state 0x10, cancel sentinel 0x100, and FUN_80059034 draw-callback binding while native window input is delivered incrementally. RosterViewer::finishRun preserves the generic loop's result code and exit status, writes current player/window/team state through commit for every non-0x100 exit, and suppresses writeback/restores the entry snapshot through cancel for 0x100. Native tests cover both sentinel repairs, both team-29 branches, constructor/input boundaries, accepted writeback, cancel suppression, and returned result/status values.

block_classifications.summary: The saved-player -1 check/reset and the two saved selection mirrors are represented by typed persistent state normalized before construction.
Saved team 29 is replaced with the active team in mode 2 and team 3 otherwise, with ordinary teams retained, exactly matching both original branches.

FUN_800590B8 construction plus FUN_8003D930 state-0x10 input/draw invocation become explicit constructor, input-state, cancel-sentinel, and callback-bound native state; generic input internals remain separately scoped.
The non-0x100 player/window/team writeback, 0x100 suppression, epilogue, and returned loop result are represented by finishRun, commit/cancel snapshots, and retained result/exit status.
